proposed_statement_changes.proposed: For fixed \(k,d_x,d_z\) and a population law \(P\), write \(M_{ZX\mid t}(P):=E_P[ZX^\top\mid T=t]\), \(M_{\mathrm{stack}}(P):=[M_{ZX\mid 0}(P)^\top,M_{ZX\mid 1}(P)^\top]^\top\), and let \(V_k(P)\) be an orthonormal basis for the population \(k\)-dimensional right singular subspace of \(M_{\mathrm{stack}}(P)\).  VMW Assumption 4 is the law-level requirement that there exist finite positive constants \(L_X,L_{ZX},L_{ZXY}\) for which \(\lVert X\rVert_2\le L_X\), \(\lVert ZX^\top\rVert_2\le L_{ZX}\), and \(\lVert YZX^\top\rVert_2\le L_{ZXY}\) almost surely under \(P\), while \(\pi(P):=\min_{t\in\{0,1\}}P(T=t)>0\) and \(\sigma(P):=\min\{\sigma_k(M_{\mathrm{stack}}(P)),\min_{t\in\{0,1\}}\sigma_k(M_{ZX\mid t}(P)V_k(P))\}>0\).  It subsequently defines \(M_X,M_Y,\kappa_B,\Gamma_X,\Gamma_Y\), and \(\kappa_{ZX}^{\star}\) as fixed derived conditioning quantities, not as additional conjunctive assumptions.  VMW Theorem 7.2 assumes Assumption 2, strict latent positivity, Assumption 4, and spectral separation, where spectral separation means \(\tau(u)\ne\tau(v)\) for distinct \(u,v\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\) and is vacuous for \(k=1\).  Together with its stated \(n,\eta\)-dependent sample-size and radius conditions, the theorem gives simultaneous high-probability finite-sample recovery of the treatment effects, the anchor-normalized feature matrix, and the simplex-projected mixture weights.  Consequently, when \(k\ge2\), a treatment-effect collision lies outside the separated recovery regime of VMW Theorem 7.2.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The existing citation gate records only spectral separation and leaves the population content of VMW Assumption 4 implicit.  The replacement narrows the gate to the source's exact fixed-dimensional population predicate, distinguishes its derived conditioning quantities from assumptions, and confines the recovery conclusion to Theorem 7.2's additional sample-dependent conditions.

source.verbatim_statement: For fixed \(k,d_x,d_z\), Assumption 4 requires finite \(L_X,L_{ZX},L_{ZXY}>0\) with \(\lVert X\rVert_2\le L_X\), \(\lVert ZX^\top\rVert_2\le L_{ZX}\), and \(\lVert YZX^\top\rVert_2\le L_{ZXY}\) almost surely; it requires \(\pi:=\min_{t\in\{0,1\}}\Pr(T=t)>0\) and, for the population right singular basis \(V_k\) of \(M_{\mathrm{stack}}\), \(\sigma:=\min\{\sigma_k(M_{\mathrm{stack}}),\min_{t\in\{0,1\}}\sigma_k(M_{ZX\mid t}V_k)\}>0\).  The displayed \(M_X,M_Y,\kappa_B,\Gamma_X,\Gamma_Y\), and \(\kappa_{ZX}^{\star}\) are then defined as fixed population conditioning quantities.  Assumption 3 requires \(\tau(u)\ne\tau(v)\) for every \(u\ne v\).  Theorem 7.2 assumes Assumption 2, strict latent positivity, Assumption 4, and spectral separation, takes the latter as vacuous when \(k=1\), imposes its displayed \(n,\eta\)-dependent radius conditions, and concludes simultaneous finite-sample bounds for the effects, anchor-normalized feature matrix, and simplex-projected mixture proportions.

prose_updates.related_work: Virk, Mazaheri, and Wu (2026, Theorem 5.4, Proposition 6.2, Assumption 4, and Theorem 7.2) provide the population operator-moment identity and the known homogeneity reduction.  In their fixed-dimensional finite-sample regime, Assumption 4 imposes finite almost-sure envelopes for \(X\), \(ZX^\top\), and \(YZX^\top\), positive marginal treatment-arm probability, and a positive population singular-value margin; its other named constants are derived conditioning quantities.  Theorem 7.2 additionally assumes proxy richness, strict latent positivity, pairwise-distinct treatment effects when \(k\ge2\), and its stated sample-dependent radius conditions before delivering high-probability treatment-effect, anchor-normalized feature-matrix, and simplex-projected mixture-weight recovery.  Their structural/finite-regularity model contains the explicit quotient collision pair because it retains full proxy rank and strict positivity without requiring distinct effects, but the collision point is outside that separated recovery theorem; the labeled witness pair is separated. Consequently, the two Le Cam converses transfer to any published-VMW comparator class containing the corresponding exact pair, with no need for whole-neighborhood containment. The gap-free positive-law modulus, estimator uppers, confidence and cluster guarantees, and matching-minimax conclusions remain on the explicitly narrower uniformly conditioned causal submodel. Mazaheri, Squires, and Uhler (2025) identify a finite latent-effect mixture through scalar synthetic moments and a Hankel pencil, without collision-uniform inference. Bauer and Fike (1960) localize spectra of perturbed diagonalizable operators, while Kato (1995, Chapter II) supplies contour-defined aggregate projectors for externally isolated clusters; neither result assigns positive causal spectral masses through a merge. Wu and Yang (2020, Sections 1, 4, and 5) project noisy summaries onto a feasible moment space before positive atomic extraction in Gaussian mixture deconvolution and inform the repair handle. Heinrich and Kahn (2018, Sections 3--5) and Ho and Nguyen (2016) analyze collision singularities for ordinary mixtures, not factorization-preserving pairs in the VMW observed proxy experiment. Deo and Randrianarisoa (2023), Robins and van der Vaart (2006), and Bing, Bunea, and Niles-Weed (2025) inform the confidence-set architecture but do not treat multiplicity of a nonnormal causal operator. Miao, Geng, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2018) motivate proxy conditional-independence and rank discipline. Van Amsterdam et al. (2022) provide the PROTECT stage-III NSCLC consumer, conditional on a separate finite-fitness and censoring bridge; their hazard model is not claimed to lie in \(\mathcal M\). Brown and Purves (1973) supply the measurable-extrema selection theorem used to choose a Borel nearest point in the compact feasible-summary closure.
